actionable_findings.title: No dedicated AI onboarding doc for adding Tauri commands, stores, or EVM/MLS features
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Create `docs/AI_ONBOARDING.md` with step-by-step checklists for adding a Tauri command, adding a store, adding an EVM contract binding, and adding an MLS feature, plus how to test each.

actionable_findings.title: Account switch races between account and ID caches
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: switch_account calls set_current_account before clearing and reloading the chat/user ID caches. Any concurrent DB operation that uses the current account and the cache could read stale cache entries against the newly selected account's database.
evidence: account_manager.rs:1260-1280: set_current_account is invoked, then db::clear_id_caches and preload run.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Clear the caches before changing the current account, or hold a single account-switch mutex so no DB operation can run between the account change and cache reload.

actionable_findings.title: SQLite connection not returned on query error
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: Functions such as get_dm_sent_received return Err before returning the connection to the pool. Because the pool holds only one connection per account, repeated errors exhaust the pool and block all subsequent DB operations.
evidence: db.rs:3128-3142: get_dm_sent_received returns the query error before return_db_connection is called.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a RAII guard that returns the connection on Drop, or use a closure pattern that always returns the connection before propagating the result.

actionable_findings.title: Edit timestamps lack millisecond precision
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: get_message_views builds edit history using event.created_at * 1000, ignoring the ms tag. Multiple edits in the same second cannot be ordered correctly and may display out of order.
evidence: db.rs:4070-4080: timestamp_ms = event.created_at * 1000 for edits, while messages use event.timestamp_ms().
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Use event.timestamp_ms() for edit timestamps, consistent with how message timestamps are reconstructed.

actionable_findings.title: EVM transactions lack explicit chain_id
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: wallet_build_and_send_transaction constructs a TransactionRequest without .with_chain_id. If the RPC provider is misconfigured or the signer is on a different network, the transaction can be signed for the wrong chain and rejected or, worse, replayed on an unintended network.
evidence: wallet_ops.rs:340-380: TransactionRequest is built with to/value/input but never chain_id.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Call .with_chain_id(net.chain_id) on the TransactionRequest before sending, and verify the returned receipt's chain_id matches.

actionable_findings.title: Auto-accept of squad channel invites based on DM content only
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: handle_text_message parses any incoming DM as a channel_in_squad invitation and auto-accepts the MLS welcome if the announcements_group_id matches a known local squad. The sender is not verified to be an admin or authorized inviter of that squad. A user who has the user's npub can send a crafted DM and force the user into a channel without consent.
evidence: lib.rs:1566-1605 `handle_text_message` auto-accepts when `parse_channel_in_squad_dm` succeeds and `in_squad` is true
lib.rs:5630-5648 `parse_channel_in_squad_dm` only validates JSON shape and type string
No check that `sender` or `contact` is an admin/member authorized to add channels to the squad
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Before auto-accepting, verify the DM sender is a member of the announcements group (or otherwise authorized) and that the channel_group_id is a valid welcome from the welcomer known to the squad.

actionable_findings.title: Giftwrap unwrap failures are silently dropped
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: handle_event matches client.unwrap_gift_wrap with Err(_) => false. A legitimate message that fails to decrypt is discarded without any log, making it impossible to debug relay or key issues.
evidence: lib.rs:1600-1605: the Err arm of unwrap_gift_wrap returns false and does not log.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Log the error reason (without message content or keys) and consider recording a metric for failed unwraps so QA can detect patterns.

actionable_findings.title: MLS live messages do not advance sync cursor
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: The live MLS group-message handler processes new messages but never writes to mls_event_cursors. The next explicit sync therefore re-fetches from the old cursor, reprocessing messages that were already handled and creating unnecessary state churn.
evidence: lib.rs:1904-2200: the notifs handler processes MLS ApplicationMessage results but never calls save_mls_event_cursor or equivalent.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: After successfully processing an MLS message, update mls_event_cursors with the latest wrapper event id and timestamp so subsequent syncs can resume from the correct position.

actionable_findings.title: Pending message ID can collide on rapid sends
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: The pending_id is derived from SystemTime::now().as_nanos(). If two messages are created in the same nanosecond, they receive the same ID, and subsequent state updates will target whichever message was found first.
evidence: message.rs:300-310: pending_id = String::from("pending-") + current_time.as_nanos().to_string().
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Include a monotonic counter or UUID in the pending ID so that two rapid sends cannot collide.

actionable_findings.title: Attachment plaintext written before dedup/reuse decision
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: The plaintext file is written to disk and the directory created before the code decides whether an existing attachment URL will be reused. This writes unencrypted data unnecessarily, wastes disk space, and may leak plaintext files even when no upload occurs.
evidence: message.rs:530-550: std::fs::create_dir_all and std::fs::write are called before will_reuse_existing is evaluated.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Move the file write to after the reuse decision and only write the plaintext when a new upload is actually required.

actionable_findings.title: MLS group creation can omit members silently
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: create_group loops over requested members and skips any whose keypackage cannot be resolved, then proceeds to create the group. The UI preflight is supposed to prevent this, but the backend still allows partial creation, which can surprise users and leave members without access.
evidence: mls.rs:350-360: missing keypackage logs a warning and continues; group creation proceeds with invited_count = member_kp_events.len().
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Return an error if any requested member cannot be resolved, making group creation atomic, or at least require explicit confirmation from the caller for partial creation.

actionable_findings.title: Local MLS group metadata deleted before leave commit is published
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: leave_group calls client.send_event and then immediately removes the group from mls_groups. If the event fails to publish, the local group is gone but the network still treats the user as a member, so the user will still receive group messages and cannot rejoin cleanly.
evidence: mls.rs:640-660: groups.retain removes the group immediately after send_event, without confirming acceptance.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the leave proposal was accepted by at least one relay before removing local metadata; on failure, return an error and keep the group.

actionable_findings.title: MLS operations re-enter Tokio runtime from blocking pool
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: send_mls_message and the live MLS handler use tokio::task::spawn_blocking and then immediately call rt.block_on. This defeats the blocking pool, risks deadlocks, and can panic when block_on is called from within the async runtime's own threads.
evidence: mls.rs:1750-1760: send_mls_message spawns a blocking task and then block_on's the async work.
lib.rs:1904-2200: notifs handler does the same for live MLS messages.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Refactor MlsService so that engine calls happen in a dedicated thread that communicates via channels, or make the engine itself Send-friendly so it can be used directly in async commands without spawn_blocking/block_on.

actionable_findings.title: Attachment filename extension from attacker-controlled tag enables path traversal
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: process_file_attachment builds the local save path from the file-type tag by calling extension_from_mime. extension_from_mime's fallback returns the raw MIME subtype, which can contain path separators (e.g., "application/../../evil"). An attacker can craft a file attachment event that writes downloaded files outside the intended vector directory.
evidence: rumor.rs:341-347 `let extension = crate::util::extension_from_mime(mime_type);` then `dir.join(format!("{}.{}, ...`
util.rs:821-836 `extension_from_mime` falls back to `lower.split('/').nth(1).unwrap_or("bin")` without sanitization
rumor.rs:363-370 `let hash_file_path = dir.join(format!("{}.{}, ox_hash, extension));`
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Sanitize the extension to only allow alphanumeric and a small allow-list of safe characters (e.g., [a-zA-Z0-9]), and validate the final path is still inside the resolved base directory before writing.

actionable_findings.title: Reactions may reference wrong message with multiple e-tags
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: process_reaction calls rumor.tags.find(TagKind::e()) which returns the first e-tag. If the reaction event references a root event plus a reply event, the reaction may be attached to the root instead of the intended message.
evidence: rumor.rs:430-440: reference_tag is the first e-tag, regardless of reply marker.
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Select the e-tag with the 'reply' marker, or fall back to the last e-tag if no marker is present, matching NIP-25 conventions.

actionable_findings.title: ChatView membership-version reactive reloads members repeatedly
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Track the last loaded version per groupId and only call `loadChannelMembers()` when `$membershipVersionByGroupId[gid]` changes.

actionable_findings.title: ChatView sends all non-inbox messages with virtualBucket 'announcements'
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Derive the `virtualBucket` from `activeChannel.name` (announcements/inbox/polls) instead of hardcoding announcements.

actionable_findings.title: DmThread side-effect reactive block processes wallet grants on every message update
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Move the wallet-grant processing into an action triggered by new messages only, and clean up pending `setDmPeerEvmAddress` promises on component unmount.

actionable_findings.title: ExportAllSecretsModal keeps decrypted secrets in component memory
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Clear the `bundle` object and `revealed` set immediately when the modal closes or on unmount; consider never storing the full bundle in a single object.

actionable_findings.title: DM load in +page.svelte is uncancellable and races on rapid conversation switches
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Track a per-npub request token or AbortController and ignore responses for conversations that are no longer active.

actionable_findings.title: Module-level Tauri listeners in profiles.ts can stack across HMR
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Register all listeners in a single async setup function with a shared `Map<string, UnlistenFn>` and call previous unlisteners before re-registering.

actionable_findings.title: AGENTS.md references a non-existent `install.sh` at the repo root
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the stale `install.sh` reference from AGENTS.md, or add the intended `install.sh` script if it is still needed.

actionable_findings.title: MessengerChatView optimistic message IDs can collide
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Include a random component in the optimistic ID, e.g. `opt-${Date.now()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`.

actionable_findings.title: DashboardPollsPanel uses unsafe cast and voids a reactive dependency
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Give `getPollBallotMap` a typed return and remove the `as Record<string, string>` cast; also remove the unnecessary `void pollBallotRefresh`.

actionable_findings.title: No Makefile, justfile, or `scripts/` directory for common development tasks
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Add a `justfile` or `scripts/dev.sh` that wraps common workflows (`pnpm tauri:dev`, `pnpm check`, `cargo test`, `pnpm test:coverage`) with consistent flags.

actionable_findings.title: Image cache SSRF protection is vulnerable to DNS rebinding
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: is_private_host only blocks obvious hostnames and literal IP addresses; it does not resolve hostnames to IP addresses. An attacker can use a hostname that resolves to a private IP (DNS rebinding) to fetch internal images or probe internal services via the image cache.
evidence: image_cache.rs:528-531 `is_private_host` blocks 'localhost', '.local', '.internal', and literal IPs but does not resolve DNS
image_cache.rs:582-587 `cache_url_image` relies on this check for SSRF protection
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the hostname before the HTTP request and reject targets that resolve to private, link-local, loopback, or CGNAT ranges; cache the resolved IP for the request lifetime.

actionable_findings.title: Relay URL validation allows arbitrary paths and query strings
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: validate_relay_url checks the scheme and host but preserves arbitrary paths and query parameters. A relay URL like wss://trusted.com/path?token=secret is accepted. This can be used to smuggle userinfo-like tokens in the path or to point to unexpected endpoints on a shared host.
evidence: lib.rs:2789-2811 `validate_relay_url` validates scheme/host/userinfo but returns `trimmed.to_string()`
lib.rs:3207-3221 `add_custom_relay` uses the raw URL after validation
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Normalize relay URLs to origin only (scheme + host + port) or explicitly reject paths, query strings, and fragments for relay entries.

actionable_findings.title: Dashboard poll vote ingestion does not verify group membership
actionable_findings.why_it_matters: process_dashboard_poll_rumor records votes using the sender's pubkey but does not verify that the sender is actually a member of the MLS group or the relevant squad. An attacker who can inject or relay a vote event can distort poll results.
evidence: rumor.rs:632-642 `process_dashboard_poll_rumor` parses vote and calls `db_apply_vote` with `voter` from `rumor.pubkey.to_bech32()`
No call to verify the voter is in the parent_id/squad membership or the MLS group
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Before applying a vote, check that the voter pubkey is a member of the parent squad/MLS group (using the existing roster tables) and that the vote is not after the poll's deadline.

actionable_findings.title: DmThread copies npub with raw navigator.clipboard and no fallback
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Use `copyTextToClipboard` from `src/lib/wallet/clipboard-copy.ts` and surface a toast when the copy fails.

actionable_findings.title: ProfileSection swallows clipboard errors when copying npub
actionable_findings.suggested_fix: Use `copyTextToClipboard` and show a toast on failure so the user knows the npub was not copied.

triage_groups.title: Cryptography and key-handling security
triage_groups.context: All secrets flow through a small set of crypto helpers and global caches; flaws here compromise every account.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix the global ENCRYPTION_KEY and hardcoded salt first (#1, #2), then replace unsafe from_utf8_unchecked (#4), then require re-auth for exports (#5), then move secret derivation into Rust (#6).
triage_groups.why: These are the highest-severity findings and share the same root cause: secrets are exposed, cached, or derived unsafely.

triage_groups.title: MLS protocol correctness
triage_groups.context: Group creation, keypackage publishing, welcome handling, and sync cursors have multiple interlocking gaps.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Implement the keypackage stub (#7), fix the kind collision (#8), clean up pending message rows (#9), then verify relay confirmation before committing group mutations (#13, #19, #20).
triage_groups.why: MLS is the core group messaging primitive; these bugs break group membership, duplicate messages, or leave stale state.

triage_groups.title: Message/event storage and deduplication
triage_groups.context: Flat event storage and in-memory state are not always consistent.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix pending row cleanup (#9), then make deduplication atomic (#11), then fix reaction/edit ordering (#24, #25) and the pending ID collision (#14).
triage_groups.why: These bugs produce duplicate messages, lost reactions, or out-of-order edits in normal chat usage.

triage_groups.title: EVM and transaction safety
triage_groups.context: Signing and transaction commands lack guardrails and explicit chain context.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Add user confirmation for signing (#6) first, then enforce chain_id on every transaction (#32), then validate addresses before use (#33).
triage_groups.why: Funds are at risk; the P1 confirmation finding is the biggest exposure.

triage_groups.title: Network and attachment SSRF / path traversal
triage_groups.context: User-supplied URLs and attachment metadata drive filesystem writes and HTTP requests.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Add SSRF protection to net.rs downloads (#16) and image_cache (#18), then sanitize attachment extensions (#12), then normalize relay URLs (#17).
triage_groups.why: These are abuse vectors that can write outside the app directory or probe internal services.

triage_groups.title: CI and quality gates
triage_groups.context: The project ships cross-platform releases without pre-merge validation.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Add a quality-gates job to CI (#36), then enable PR builds (#37), then remove the MCP bridge from release deps (#38), then fix the updater endpoint (#43).
triage_groups.why: Without CI gates, the highest-impact fixes above cannot be verified automatically.

triage_groups.title: Frontend architecture and store lifecycle
triage_groups.context: Large components, uncancellable loads, and store cross-talk create a brittle shell.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Reset the profiles store on logout (#48), validate Tauri payloads (#49), then decompose the largest components (#50, #51, #52, #53, #54) and fix the DM load races (#55).
triage_groups.why: These affect user-visible reliability and make the codebase hard for AI and humans to reason about.

triage_groups.title: Project hygiene and AI onboarding
triage_groups.context: Legacy references, missing docs, and tooling gaps slow contributors.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix the ALCHEMY_ env prefix leak (#63), remove legacy-fix docs (#64), update deep-link scheme (#65), add an AI onboarding doc (#67), and add a justfile (#68).
triage_groups.why: These are low-risk but high-leverage for development velocity.

residual_risks: MLS engine (mdk-core / mdk-sqlite-storage) is a git dependency at a fixed commit; its cryptography, downgrade handling, and replay protection were not audited in this pass.
NIP-17 giftwrap security relies entirely on nostr-sdk; key compromise of a relay or relay MITM could expose metadata even if payload content is encrypted.
The global MNEMONIC_SEED is held as a standard String; the Rust allocator may move or copy it, and no secure zeroization is performed after logout or key derivation.
No rate limiting or key-derivation throttling on PIN unlock; an attacker with local filesystem access can attempt many PINs against the Argon2-derived key.
No certificate pinning for RPC, Blossom, or relay endpoints; a compromised system CA or local MITM can intercept traffic or return malicious payloads.
The ENCRYPTION_KEY is cached for the process lifetime and never rotated; legacy data encrypted under a weak or leaked PIN cannot be re-keyed.

The global ChatState (STATE) is a single tokio::sync::Mutex that is acquired frequently and held across async operations. Under heavy load or with many concurrent chats this could become a bottleneck or cause head-of-line blocking; a per-chat lock or actor model would reduce contention but requires a larger refactor.

The in-memory WRAPPER_ID_CACHE is cleared when sync finishes. A duplicate wrapper received after the cache is cleared but before the DB dedup path is exercised could be processed twice, leading to duplicate UI entries until the DB check catches it.

Reaction processing in lib.rs drops reactions whose referenced message is not yet in state. The TODO at lib.rs:1810 acknowledges this, but there is no persistent queue, so reactions received ahead of their messages during a partial sync are permanently lost.

Network errors in net.rs and wallet_ops.rs are swallowed or converted to boolean/String without structured retry metadata. This makes it hard to distinguish transient failures from permanent ones and can lead to silent data staleness in wallet balances and attachment reuse decisions.

The Nostr client (NOSTR_CLIENT) is a global std::sync::RwLock. While get_nostr_client clones the Arc without holding the lock, set/clear panic on poison and there is no explicit lifetime management across account switches. A poisoned lock after a panic would render the client unreachable.
Tauri event name casing/hyphenation (e.g. `typing-update`) cannot be fully verified from the frontend; a mismatch with Rust would silently drop typing events.
Plaintext localStorage caches for wallet summaries, Safe state, and treasury infra are scoped by npub but remain unencrypted; device access can leak account metadata.
Module-level listeners in `src/stores/profiles.ts` are assumed to be reset by the backend restart on logout; if logout ever stops restarting the app, listeners will continue updating stores.
Concurrent `parent-map-disk-cache.ts` read/write cycles could interleave if multiple dashboard fetches for the same parent race.
Svelte 5 legacy reactive semantics may cause subtle re-run bugs in components with many `$:` side-effect blocks.
MCP bridge crate may still be compiled and linked into release binaries even though the code path is cfg-gated, because it is a non-optional dependency in Cargo.toml.
Auto-updater endpoint references the legacy `covenant-application` repository, which may cause update checks to fail or return stale artifacts.
Release notes are a hard-coded placeholder and every release is drafted, so users see no changelog until a human manually edits the release.
Legacy `vector://` and `vectorapp.io` deep-link/relay references remain in the codebase, risking brand confusion and broken protocol handlers.
No pre-merge CI means regressions can reach `main` and immediately trigger a cross-platform release build.
AI contributors rely on AGENTS.md and scattered docs; there is no single onboarding checklist for common tasks.
testing_gaps: No unit tests for crypto.rs behavior with malformed, non-UTF-8, or truncated ciphertext; unsafe/from_utf8_unchecked path is untested.
No tests verifying that the Argon2 salt is unique per install or that two identical PINs produce different keys.
No tests for account key isolation: switching accounts should not decrypt one account's secrets with another account's key.
No tests for path traversal in attachment extension handling (e.g., MIME subtype containing '..' or path separators).
No tests for SSRF in attachment downloads or net.rs; private IP ranges, DNS rebinding, and URL scheme validation are not exercised.
No tests for authorization on export commands (get_seed, export_evm_account_key_plaintext) requiring re-authentication.
No tests for EVM signing and transaction confirmation boundaries; commands can be invoked without a PIN in tests.
No tests for auto-accept of channel-in-squad invites verifying the sender's authorization.
No unit tests for ChatState message ordering, duplicate handling, or reaction application under concurrent additions.
No tests verifying that pending message rows are cleaned up after a successful send.
No tests for the MLS keypackage publish path; the stub currently makes the feature untestable.
No tests for sync cursor advancement after live MLS message processing.
No tests for the DB connection return-on-error invariant, which would catch the leak identified in get_dm_sent_received.
No tests that verify send_event_to success list behavior for MLS and DM sends.
No tests for hex_string_to_bytes malformed input behavior.
No integration tests for account switching that verify cache consistency and connection pool state.
No unit tests for `subscribeAppEvents` event routing, listener cleanup, or payload validation.
No tests that verify `clearAccountState` clears every account-scoped store, including `profiles` and `profileLoadingStates`.
No tests for DM/channel message-load cancellation and ordering when the user switches conversations rapidly.
No tests for export-modals clearing secrets from component memory on close and unmount.
No tests for `getInvokeErrorMessage` / `friendlyMessage` mapping for backend auth and DM-send errors.
No tests for `currentNpubForPersistence` scoping: stores must not write to localStorage when the current npub is null or changed.
CI does not run `pnpm test` or `cargo test`.
No integration tests for Tauri commands; frontend unit tests only mock `invoke` from `@tauri-apps/api/core`.
Svelte components are excluded from the Vitest coverage report (`src/**/*.svelte`), so UI coverage is unknown.
No end-to-end harness exists; the self-correcting AI testing plan is documented but not implemented.
High-risk Rust modules (`mls.rs`, `message.rs`, `chat.rs`, `account_manager.rs`, `evm/wallet_ops.rs`, `evm/advanced_contract_call.rs`, `voice.rs`, `net.rs`) have little or no test coverage.
No Cargo `[dev-dependencies]` for test helpers (e.g., tempfile, tokio-test, pretty_assertions).
